SMTO-EXE-0224 — SMTO couldn't find that Docker image

GUID: f32b614d-b319-5e6b-a365-1e3543671f3c
Slug: docker-image-not-found
Domain: EXE · Subsystem: docker

What happened

  • The Docker image you named (the package Docker uses to start a container) isn't on the Gateway computer, or in the online registry, under exactly that name and tag. Nothing was changed.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Ask SMTO to list the Docker images on that Gateway, and compare the exact name and tag (the part after the colon, such as :1.0 or :latest). SMTO only accepts an exact match, so myapp and myapp:1.0 count as different images.
  2. If you asked SMTO to download (pull) the image, check its exact name and tag on the website of the registry it comes from. If the registry has nothing under that name, the download finds nothing.
  3. If the image needs to be built or downloaded first, ask SMTO for that step only if you really need a new image. Building or downloading adds an image to that computer, so it should be your deliberate choice.

What success looks like

  • SMTO finds the image by its exact name and tag, and the action completes.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them, with the image name you used, to the person who manages Docker on that computer.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Exact image resolution found no image whose ID or tag matches the reference exactly, or the Docker Engine returned 404 on an /images endpoint, including a pull of a reference the registry does not have.

What this means

  • Exact image lookup found no matching full identity/tag, or an image endpoint returned not found. Docker execution remains on the selected Gateway and its explicitly configured local Engine. Preserve accepted private references, exact object identities, completed prefixes and unknown effects; diagnostics never replay a mutation.

Why this can happen

  • Exact image lookup found no matching full identity/tag, or an image endpoint returned not found.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect exact image IDs/tags and whether the failure concerns local lookup or a registry-facing image request.

How to fix it

  • List images on the same Gateway (docker images --no-trunc as the Gateway account) and use the full image ID or an exact repository:tag; pulls default to the latest tag only when none is given. For pulls, confirm the reference exists in the registry, and build or pull only when that is intended.
  • Correct the exact image reference or establish its availability through an authorized pull/build only when needed.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect the exact object identity, typed arguments and selected Gateway capability; correct the reported prerequisite before a new request.

How to verify the fix

  • The intended image reference resolves at the required operation boundary.

What not to do

  • Never automatically replay an uncertain Docker mutation.

Technical notes

  • Docker execution remains on the selected Gateway and its explicitly configured local Engine. Preserve accepted private references, exact object identities, completed prefixes and unknown effects; diagnostics never replay a mutation.
